key_insight: Wall-resolved LES shows that the DTU 10-MW airfoil’s separation-bubble dynamics are dominated by a Kelvin-Helmholtz wavepacket, while the long-time lift/normal-force response exhibits a slow low-frequency oscillation.
engineering_relevance: These results help predict transition, separation, and unsteady loading on wind-turbine blades, informing airfoil design and aeroelastic/load mitigation.
method: Wall-resolved LES with Nek5000 and EllipSys at Re_c = 1e5 and AoA = 3.1°–3.3°
Cross-code validation against Nek5000, plus PSE and SPOD to identify instability modes
Long-time EllipSys simulations to quantify low-frequency force modulation
evidence_signal: A 10% chord spanwise domain reproduced the mean flow and dominant disturbances, and EllipSys agreed closely with Nek5000 except for underpredicted Tollmien-Schlichting amplitudes.
watch_item: EllipSys’s higher numerical dissipation can suppress attached-boundary-layer TS-wave amplitude, so fine-scale transition predictions may be code- and resolution-sensitive.
paper_title: Numerical simulations of transition and long-term response of a wind turbine airfoil
